headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from MemMachine’s MCP/API surfaces paired with a non-egress Spring integration sample; no direct evidence of shared workspace or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can ingest external content through agentic channels; spring-integration-samples has no documented protections or provenance controls. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default integrations if Spring forwards MemMachine outputs into a parser or prompt, but the exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty stays at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Spring Integration forwards MemMachine output into an LLM prompt or tool parser without sanitization, injection is reachable.
IF a shared MCP or message channel is configured between the two agents, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from MemMachine outputs.
Add provenance tags and strip instruction-like text before parsing.
Route outputs through a human review step for high-impact actions.
Use allowlisted schemas for any MCP messages.
requires-engineering: add content-isolation and provenance enforcement at the orchestrator layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while spring-integration-samples has no declared data handling or isolation. If they share a workspace or Spring relays MemMachine context to logs, files, or downstream services, sensitive conversational data can leak; the profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same workspace or log sink, MemMachine context can be exposed to Spring-side consumers.
IF Spring serializes MemMachine prompts or memory into outbound messages, user facts may leave the intended boundary.
mitigations: Turn off verbose logging for both agents.
Keep MemMachine memory stores separate from Spring runtime files.
Redact personal facts before passing data across the boundary.
Restrict outbound destinations to approved endpoints only.
requires-engineering: implement per-agent data partitioning and retention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and MCP/API surfaces, while spring-integration-samples shows no write, network, or OAuth scopes. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so a write conflict is not evidenced; the only plausible conflict is unusual orchestration that shares a writable directory or queue.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or queue, file/message races can occur.
IF an orchestrator grants shared mutable state, one agent may overwrite the other's artifacts.
mitigations: Place each agent in its own working directory.
Disable shared write access to git or filesystem state.
Use file locks if a shared artifact is unavoidable.
Separate credentials and API tokens per agent.
requires-engineering: add concurrency control for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can produce memory-backed outputs through REST, SDK, or MCP, and spring-integration-samples is an integration framework that may consume upstream outputs. If Spring treats MemMachine responses as authoritative without validation, errors can cascade into downstream actions; the pair lacks documented verification steps, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Spring uses MemMachine output as a source of truth without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF downstream handlers trigger bookings, messages, or state changes from those facts, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Add a validation step before any downstream action.
Require source citations for factual claims.
Use confidence thresholds and fallback to manual review.
Log and diff MemMachine outputs before execution.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, but neither profile shows regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies. spring-integration-samples has no declared compliance surface. With no documented mismatch, compliance risk is limited to undocumented deployment choices, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through MemMachine and stored in a jurisdictionally restricted deployment, residency issues can arise.
IF Spring logs the same data class under a different retention policy, compliance drift becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Document retention settings for both runtimes.
Disable or minimize logs containing user facts.
Review deployment region and data-processing terms.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
